title: Legacy client request/response translation gateway for Chat Completions compatibility
creator: Asha Patel
description: Implement a translation gateway that maps Redwood Inference request/response shapes to the OpenAI Chat Completions semantics for legacy clients. The gateway must: (1) accept Redwood API shapes and emit OpenAI-compatible requests when routed to backends expecting Chat Completions; (2) translate streamed delta events (including partial function_call payloads) back into Redwood streaming frames; (3) normalize structured outputs and function-calling signals into Redwood's structured-output schema; (4) preserve telemetry, cost attribution, and per-token latency signals; and (5) offer per-customer opt-in toggles and a staged rollout plan. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, integration tests, and rollout orchestration for the gateway proxy layer.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway accepts Redwood /chat request and generates an OpenAI Chat Completions-compatible payload (roles, content blocks, system/user/assistant semantics)
Streaming responses: gateway correctly merges OpenAI-style delta events (content_delta + function_call fragments) into Redwood streaming frames with identical ordering guarantees

Function/tool calling: both explicit function responses and model-initiated function_call events are surfaced to Redwood SDKs as structured outputs, with metadata for call name, args (partial/merged), and call status
Structured output alignment: JSON-schema outputs returned by models are validated and rewritten (or annotated) to match Redwood's structured-output contract without dropping unknown fields
Backcompat modes: gateway supports two modes — strict-oa-emulation and permissive-redwood — toggleable per org
End-to-end tests exercising network-level streaming, timeouts, retries, and malformed partial-chunks pass in CI
tasks: Spike: enumerate differences between Redwood request schema and OpenAI Chat Completions (2025/2026 variants)
Design spec: define mapping table for fields, streaming frames, and error mapping (Confluence doc)
Prototype: implement a lightweight HTTP proxy that rewrites requests/responses and supports SSE and chunked transfer streaming
Integration tests: simulate OpenAI streaming deltas including partial function_call fragments and out-of-order chunks
Telemetry: ensure per-token cost and latency attribution is preserved and added to request-level traces
Rollout: create feature-flagged rollout with canary customers and automatic rollback on error budget impact
comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha Patel: Spike complete. Found 3 key mismatch classes: role naming, streaming fragment envelopes, and function_call partials. Prototype approach looks feasible using a stateful per-request assembler.

2026-02-24 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented initial assembler for function_call fragments. Edge case: some OpenAI-style streams send function_call.args in multiple interleaved chunks with escaped JSON—need robust incremental JSON reassembly and guarded parsing.

2026-03-01 - PM review (Lina Chen): Asked for clear behavior when model returns invalid JSON for structured outputs. Decision: gateway will preserve original raw output as a fallback field (raw_output) and raise a structured_output_parsing warning in telemetry.

2026-03-04 - Security (Omar Farouk): Requested threat model writeup for header and auth passthrough. Action: do not forward customer tokens to third-party backends; use Redwood service identity and maintain org token mapping in vault. Marked security_review_required=true.

2026-03-08 - Eng review (Sophie Meyer): Performance note: initial proxy added ~8ms p50 per-request. Optimize by avoiding JSON reserialization when mapping is identity. Tracing hooks added to measure delta assembly time.

2026-03-10 - Marco Ruiz: Integration tests for streaming deltas added. Observed a race where streaming SSE resets after 1MB chunk boundary on a specific client; added rebuffering logic and test vector.
notes: Trade-offs: doing translation at proxy layer minimizes client changes but adds operational complexity and latency. Alternative was server-side multi-shape support in runtime — bigger refactor and higher risk during rollout.

Fallback strategy: when structured-output validation fails, return original model output with structured_output=null and include parse_error in response metadata. This keeps legacy clients functioning.
Observability: add per-request assembly logs (sampled) and a dashboard showing assembly errors and function_call reassembly latency by model/back-end
